items.title: Bipartisan momentum builds behind the Clarity Act
points: A Democratic lawmaker joined Republicans in backing the Clarity Act (proposed U.S. legislation that would define which federal agency regulates which crypto assets, giving the industry legal certainty).
American Bankers Association CEO said there is 'a lot of good' in the proposal, signaling traditional banking sector support.
SoFi CEO urged Congress to 'pass it immediately,' showing fintech alignment on the need for regulatory clarity.
Combined bank and fintech backing suggests the bill has unusually broad industry support for a crypto measure.

items.title: Emirates to accept Bitcoin for flight bookings
points: Emirates airline will let customers pay for flight tickets in Bitcoin, one of the largest travel-sector crypto integrations to date.
The move signals merchant adoption at scale rather than niche crypto-only retailers.

items.title: Coldcard wallet flaw drains $38M in Bitcoin in 25 minutes
points: 594 BTC (~$38M) was stolen from 500 wallets in 25 minutes via a flaw in seed generation (the process that turns randomness into a wallet's private keys).
The bug made private keys (the cryptographic secrets that control funds) more predictable than intended, letting attackers guess and sweep balances.
Maker Coinkite suspects the attacker used AI to analyze older open-source firmware versions to find the exploit.
Coinkite published its advisory only after the theft, too late for affected users.
The case challenges the assumption that open-source code is inherently safer, since public code is now easily auditable by AI-powered attackers.

items.title: Zcash patches critical Orchard privacy flaw
points: A security researcher found a critical vulnerability in Zcash's Orchard shielded pool (the system that hides sender, receiver and amount in transactions).
Zcash activated its Ironwood upgrade within days of disclosure to fix the issue.
Coming alongside the Coldcard breach, it has pushed crypto firms into broader code audits over AI-driven exploit risk.

items.title: Circle wins New York trust charter
points: Circle, issuer of the USDC stablecoin (a token designed to hold a constant $1 value), received a New York trust charter.
It follows a recent federal approval for a national trust bank license, widening Circle's regulatory permissions.

items.title: Coinbase misses Q2 expectations
points: Coinbase posted lower Q2 revenue and a net loss as crypto trading activity declined.
Subscription and lending segments grew but not enough to offset weaker trading fees.

items.title: Luno cuts 20% of staff
points: Exchange Luno laid off 20% of its global workforce, citing automation.
The CEO framed the cuts as a pivot from retail trading toward institutional infrastructure.
